title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for diabetes management.

HPI
The patient presents today for a routine follow-up regarding their type 2 diabetes. They report feeling generally well but note recent fatigue. They have been taking their oral hypoglycemic medication consistently for several years. The patient reports that their blood glucose readings have been elevated recently.

Medication List
Metformin 500mg BID.

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented. Skin is intact without acute lesions. Vital signs are stable. Physical examination of the extremities shows no acute distress.

Assessment
The patient has type 2 diabetes mellitus. Current laboratory results indicate hyperglycemia. The patient's glucose levels appear poorly controlled at this time despite adherence to the current medication regimen.

Plan
Continue current dose of metformin. We will monitor glucose levels closely and may consider adjusting the dosage of the oral medication. The patient was instructed to monitor home glucose readings more frequently and return for a follow-up in four weeks.
explanations: Diabetes documented as poorly controlled, out of control, or with hyperglycemia is coded to diabetes with hyperglycemia.
Long-term oral hypoglycemic use: add Z79.84.

distractors.why: Hyperglycemia is a complication with its own code.
Z79.84 captures long-term oral hypoglycemic use.
